what: Friendface 2 against Tracker Cleaner (the version is under "extension") with the cross-site-id counter-repair (C33) and the page shield (C32, on by default from 1.26) fully on. A value detector learns a value is cross-site only after two sites have sent it, so the collector receives the id on first contact and the initial cross-site JOIN happens once and cannot be undone; from then on the cleaner blocks the exact collector path (/f/, never the site root) and strips confirmed ids from URLs and links, so no further send gets through. Separately, M4 makes the shield blur the font-measure widths and screen size, so the F6 fingerprint join key no longer matches across sites or a cleaner-off baseline. The fingerprint is measured with the shield off (baseline) and on.
headline: 10/10 kinds joined on first contact (a value detector cannot prevent that); going forward the cleaner stops 6/10 (collector path blocked, incl. the ETag image under /f/; the per-site cookie F1 that the collector path set is deleted) and 4/10 survive (F3, F4, F5, F7: first-party server-side F4/F5, sign-in F7, hand-off chain F3).
caveats: Lab-only: loopback, made-up names, fake accounts; nothing leaves the machine.

A value-based cross-site detector is reactive: the collector gets the id on first contact, before two sites reveal it is cross-site, so the initial join is not preventable; the cleaner stops every FURTHER send by blocking the exact collector path (never the site root) and stripping the id from request URLs and links.
F4/F5 and F8-to-the-site's-own-server are first-party server-side; they cannot be stopped without breaking the site, so they are marked "cannot", not blocked.

F1 (N2, 1.28): the per-site cookie fp_id is not a cross-site value itself, but it was SET by the path that is confirmed as a first-party collector of one, so it is deleted there (names noted in memory only; undoable for 10 minutes; never a sign-in cookie). Measured from the browser's cookies and from what the frozen ff2 server receives afterwards (see f1). F7 is a sign-in cookie: left alone on purpose. F3 (the hand-off chain) is per-site here, not a confirmed cross-site value. F10 (ETag) is per-site here and its image /f/px.gif is under the blocked /f/ path, so it is stopped going forward; M5 additionally strips the If-None-Match conditional for a cross-site ETag id on a resource that is not otherwise blocked (not exercised by ff2, whose ETag is per-site).

The shield (C32) is ON by default from 1.26 (M4). It now blurs the font-measure widths and screen size (not only canvas/WebGL/audio), so the F6 join key -- built from fonts and matchMedia/screen -- no longer matches across the three sites or the cleaner-off baseline when the shield is on. matchMedia and the pixel ratio are left alone (a page needs them), so it is best effort, detectable, not perfect. The collector-path block (C33) already stops the code reaching the collector as well.

rows.why: stopped going forward: the cookie fp_id that the confirmed collector path /f/ set was deleted on all three sites (atlas.localhost fp_id, ledger.localhost fp_id, sundial.localhost fp_id; each can be put back for 10 minutes), the site's own server no longer receives it (its "What I know" finds no browser on any of the three sites), and /f/ is blocked so it is not set again. Ledger's went 296 s after the counter-repair was restored: deleting was held for that site for five minutes after its sign-in page (step 8)
stopped going forward: the master id reaches the collector is blocked (collector-path block, host+/f/ prefix)

survives: M3 strips a CONFIRMED id from a scripted/meta/pushState hand-off, but ff2 gives each site its own master value at /f/ (ledger/sundial/atlas each send a different ff2m-...), so no single master value is seen on two sites and none is confirmed; the real cross-site link is the fingerprint, whose collector send is already blocked
survives: the from->to redirect log is the site's own server; cannot stop without breaking navigation
survives: a first-party click record on the site's own server; cannot stop without breaking the site
stopped going forward: the fingerprint code reaches the collector is blocked (collector-path block, host+/f/ prefix)
survives: a sign-in cookie (SID): kept on purpose, never touched
stopped going forward: the address and referrer are posted to the collector is blocked (collector-path block, host+/f/ prefix)
stopped going forward: the collector runs its loopback probe for the page is blocked (collector-path block, host+/f/ prefix)

stopped going forward: its ETag image /f/px.gif is under the blocked collector path, so the browser no longer revalidates it with If-None-Match (M5 also strips the conditional for a cross-site ETag on a resource that is not otherwise blocked)
